title: Time Jump: 11:45, Gas Crew Digging, Families at the Gate

fields.narration: EXERCISE. THIS IS NOT A SAFETY EVALUATION OF ANY REAL STRUCTURE. It is now 11:45 on Wednesday, April 14, 2027. The Valley Gas truck pulled in at the west gate at 11:43. Its crew is hand-digging at 16+00 to squeeze off the torn service line. The gas has not stopped and you can still hear it. Luis Marquez has been buried for 85 minutes. The muddy water is now above his waist. From the top of the ladder, Rescue 2 medics are passing him oxygen and a warming blanket. He is still talking to them. The second worker, the helper for E-7 operator Gordon Pruitt, left for the regional trauma center by ambulance at 10:52. The community hotline has taken 34 calls. Cars are lining Corliss Avenue, and people are walking up to the west gate asking for 'the boss.' The Dayton Ledger's noon deadline is 15 minutes away, and the Channel 9 helicopter is still overhead. On the trailer 2 display, CG-3 has held at 0.26 inches since 11:05. The print shop, the apartment house and the church hall preschool are still empty, and the fire department controls them. Take a moment to bring your logs up to this time. Then we continue.
worldState: Clock: 11:45, Wednesday, April 14, 2027. Overcast, ground saturated, light west-southwest wind still pushing gas east toward the trailer compound and Ninth Street.
Ninth Street Command (Dayton Fire Department battalion chief, west gate, Corliss Avenue and Ninth Street) holds command of the rescue. No Larkspur employee goes past the fire tape.
The Valley Gas crew arrived at 11:43 and is hand-digging at 16+00 to squeeze off the service. The gas leak is not controlled yet, and the 4-inch main upstream still reads 55 psi.
Rescue 2 will not start shoring or put anyone in the trench until the gas line is squeezed off and meter readings at the 16+00 end allow it.

Luis Marquez has been buried to the chest since 10:20 (85 minutes). Water is above his waist and still rising with the pump shut down. He is conscious and receiving oxygen and a warming blanket from medics at the top of the ladder.
The E-7 operator's helper (left forearm injury, bleeding) left by ambulance for the regional trauma center at 10:52. His admission status has not been reported to Larkspur.

Standby equipment in the east staging yard is unused: two aluminum hydraulic shores, the spare 10-by-20-foot trench box and the standby excavator. Ninth Street Command has said it may ask for them at the 14+00 end once the gas is controlled, and has asked that nothing move yet.
The community hotline has taken 34 calls since the incident began. Several callers say they are workers' relatives asking whether their family member is the one buried.
Family members and onlookers are parking along Corliss Avenue and coming to the west gate on foot asking for 'the boss.'
The Dayton Ledger reporter files at 12:00 with or without a Larkspur statement. The Channel 9 helicopter is still circling.

CG-3 (Harlan & Weir south foundation) has held at 0.26 in since 11:05, above the 0.25 in action level. The print shop, the apartment house and the Ninth Street Church hall preschool are empty under fire department control.
fields.facilitatorNote: Check that each role writes the 11:45 status in the incident log and that the superintendent stays at Ninth Street Command as the single liaison. Watch for the Safety Director and Project Manager setting up a family meeting point away from the west gate and the fire line, and for the Project Executive deciding on a Ledger statement before noon that confirms no names or casualty counts. If anyone asks about OSHA, the 24-hour reporting clock starts only if the helper is formally admitted as an in-patient, so the team should be finding out his status. Credit a crew staged next to the equipment and ready to go. Push back if anyone moves equipment or touches Valley Gas valves.
